rules.title: HTML5 doctype present as first line
rules.what_to_look_for: The very first non-whitespace bytes of the raw HTML document. Look for the literal string <!doctype html> (case-insensitive) before any other markup, comment, or content.
rules.pass_when: The document begins with <!doctype html> (case-insensitive, no legacy public/system identifiers) before any element or text node.
rules.fail_when: The doctype is missing, malformed, a legacy/quirks-triggering doctype, or preceded by content other than whitespace/BOM (which triggers quirks mode).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the first line of the raw HTML source, e.g. <!doctype html>.

rules.title: Valid lang attribute on <html>
rules.what_to_look_for: The <html> root element's lang attribute. Inspect its value and confirm it is a well-formed BCP 47 language tag (e.g. en, en-US, fr-CA).
rules.pass_when: <html> has a non-empty lang attribute whose value is a syntactically valid BCP 47 tag.
rules.fail_when: The lang attribute is absent, empty, or not a valid BCP 47 tag (e.g. lang="english").
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the opening <html ...> tag showing the lang value.

rules.title: UTF-8 charset declared early in <head>
rules.what_to_look_for: A <meta charset="utf-8"> element inside <head>, appearing within the first 1024 bytes of the document. Confirm the declared encoding is UTF-8.
rules.pass_when: <meta charset="utf-8"> (case-insensitive) appears within the first 1024 bytes of the response body, before any non-ASCII content.
rules.fail_when: No charset meta exists, it declares a non-UTF-8 encoding, or it appears after the first 1024 bytes.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <meta charset=...> tag and note its byte position in the head.

rules.title: Responsive viewport meta without scaling lock
rules.what_to_look_for: A <meta name="viewport"> element in <head> with content including width=device-width. Check for any user-scaling restrictions: user-scalable=no or maximum-scale set below 5.
rules.pass_when: <meta name="viewport"> exists with content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" (or equivalent) and does NOT disable zoom (no user-scalable=no, no maximum-scale<5).
rules.fail_when: The viewport meta is missing, omits width=device-width, or disables/limits user scaling (user-scalable=no or maximum-scale<5).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the full <meta name="viewport" content="..."> tag.

rules.title: Exactly one non-empty <title> in <head>
rules.what_to_look_for: The <title> element(s) inside <head>. Count occurrences and inspect the text content for non-whitespace characters.
rules.pass_when: Exactly one <title> element exists in <head> and its text content is non-empty (more than whitespace).
rules.fail_when: Zero <title> elements, more than one <title>, an empty <title></title>, or a title outside <head>.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <title>...</title> element and its text content.

rules.title: Unique meta description summary present
rules.what_to_look_for: A <meta name="description"> element in <head> with a non-empty, page-specific content attribute serving as a search/social snippet.
rules.pass_when: <meta name="description" content="..."> exists with a concise, non-empty, page-relevant summary.
rules.fail_when: The description meta is missing, has empty content, or is a generic boilerplate string reused identically site-wide.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <meta name="description" content="..."> tag.

rules.title: Canonical URL declared via rel=canonical
rules.what_to_look_for: A <link rel="canonical" href="..."> element in <head>. Confirm the href is a single absolute URL.
rules.pass_when: Exactly one <link rel="canonical"> exists in <head> with an absolute href pointing to the preferred URL of the page.
rules.fail_when: No rel=canonical link exists, multiple conflicting canonical links exist, or the href is empty/relative/invalid.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <link rel="canonical" href="..."> tag.

rules.title: Favicon and app icon set declared
rules.what_to_look_for: In <head>: a <link rel="icon"> (ideally an SVG via type="image/svg+xml"), an ICO fallback (rel="icon" at /favicon.ico or default), an <link rel="apple-touch-icon">, and a maskable PWA icon referenced in the web app manifest.
rules.pass_when: At least an SVG/ICO favicon plus an apple-touch-icon are declared, with a maskable icon defined in the linked manifest.
rules.fail_when: No favicon link present and no /favicon.ico fallback, or apple-touch-icon and maskable PWA icon both absent.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <link rel="icon">, <link rel="apple-touch-icon">, and the manifest icon entry.

rules.title: theme-color meta for browser chrome
rules.what_to_look_for: One or more <meta name="theme-color"> elements in <head>, ideally paired with a media attribute (e.g. media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)") for light/dark variants.
rules.pass_when: <meta name="theme-color" content="..."> exists with a valid CSS color; bonus when separate light/dark variants use the media attribute.
rules.fail_when: No theme-color meta is present, or its content is not a valid CSS color value.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote each <meta name="theme-color" ...> tag including any media attribute.

rules.title: color-scheme meta declared
rules.what_to_look_for: A <meta name="color-scheme"> element in <head> (or a CSS color-scheme property) whose content lists supported schemes, e.g. content="light dark".
rules.pass_when: <meta name="color-scheme" content="..."> declares the supported schemes (e.g. "light dark" or "dark"), enabling native dark rendering without a flash.
rules.fail_when: No color-scheme declaration exists in the meta or root CSS, leaving the browser to default and risk a white flash in dark mode.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <meta name="color-scheme" content="..."> tag.

rules.title: Open Graph core tags present
rules.what_to_look_for: <meta property="og:..."> tags in <head>: og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url, og:type. Confirm each has non-empty content and og:image/og:url are absolute URLs.
rules.pass_when: All five core OG tags (og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url, og:type) are present with valid non-empty content.
rules.fail_when: Any of the five core OG tags is missing or empty, or og:image/og:url is not an absolute URL.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote each <meta property="og:..." content="..."> tag.

rules.title: Feed discovery via rel=alternate link
rules.what_to_look_for: A <link rel="alternate"> in <head> with a feed type — type="application/rss+xml", "application/atom+xml", or "application/feed+json" — and an href to the feed.
rules.pass_when: At least one <link rel="alternate"> with an RSS/Atom/JSON feed type and a valid href is declared in <head>.
rules.fail_when: No feed-typed <link rel="alternate"> exists, or the href is missing/invalid, leaving the feed undiscoverable.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <link rel="alternate" type="..." href="..."> tag.

rules.title: Feed document well-formed and self-describing
rules.what_to_look_for: Fetch the feed URL from rel=alternate and parse it: an atom:link rel="self", a stable unique guid/id per item, valid date/update fields, and overall well-formed XML/JSON that passes feed validation.
rules.pass_when: The feed parses cleanly, includes atom:link rel="self", every item has a stable unique guid/id, and dates/update cadence are valid.
rules.fail_when: The feed is malformed, missing atom:link rel="self", has unstable or duplicate item guids, or fails feed validation.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the feed's atom:link rel="self" element and a representative <item>/<entry> guid.

rules.title: Native Popover API used for transient UI
rules.what_to_look_for: In the markup, elements bearing the popover attribute and corresponding popovertarget invokers (or popovertargetaction), used for modals/menus/tooltips instead of hand-rolled ARIA-managed JS overlays.
rules.pass_when: Transient top-layer UI (menus, tooltips, dialogs) uses the native popover attribute with popovertarget invokers.
rules.fail_when: Such UI is built solely from custom JS show/hide with manual ARIA wiring and no use of the native popover attribute where it would apply.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote an element with the popover attribute and its popovertarget invoker button.

rules.title: robots.txt present and parseable at site root
rules.what_to_look_for: GET /robots.txt at the site root; response status, Content-Type, and body. Body should be plain text with at least one valid group (a User-agent: line followed by Allow:/Disallow: directives), per RFC 9309. Optionally a Sitemap: line.
rules.pass_when: GET /robots.txt returns 200 with a text/plain (or text-like) body containing at least one valid 'User-agent:' directive and well-formed Allow/Disallow lines.
rules.fail_when: GET /robots.txt returns 404/410, returns HTML instead of plain text, returns 5xx, or the body is not parseable as RFC 9309 (no valid User-agent group).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the response status line, the Content-Type header, and the first few directive lines of the body (e.g. 'User-agent: *', 'Disallow: /admin').

rules.title: XML sitemap present listing canonical URLs
rules.what_to_look_for: A sitemap.xml (at /sitemap.xml or the path declared in robots.txt 'Sitemap:'). Root element <urlset> in the sitemaps.org namespace with <url><loc> entries holding absolute canonical URLs; optional <lastmod> per entry.
rules.pass_when: Sitemap is reachable, is valid XML with a <urlset> root in the sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9 namespace, and contains at least one <url><loc> with an absolute URL.
rules.fail_when: No sitemap is reachable, the document is not valid XML, the root is not <urlset>/<sitemapindex>, or there are zero <loc> entries.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the sitemap URL, the <urlset> opening tag with its xmlns, and one or two <url><loc>...</loc><lastmod>...</lastmod></url> entries.

rules.title: Sitemap index used when split across multiple sitemaps
rules.what_to_look_for: A <sitemapindex> root element (sitemaps.org namespace) containing <sitemap><loc> child sitemap URLs, used when the URL set exceeds 50000 URLs / 50MB or is split by content type.
rules.pass_when: Either the site fits in a single <urlset> sitemap (<=50000 URLs), or a <sitemapindex> exists with one or more <sitemap><loc> child entries that each resolve to a valid sub-sitemap.
rules.fail_when: A single sitemap exceeds 50000 <url> entries (or ~50MB) with no <sitemapindex> aggregating split sitemaps, or a <sitemapindex> lists child <loc> entries that 404/are not valid sitemaps.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <sitemapindex> opening tag and one <sitemap><loc>...</loc></sitemap> child, or the URL count of the single sitemap that proves no index is needed.

rules.title: Image/video sitemap extension namespaces used for media metadata
rules.what_to_look_for: In the <urlset>, the image (xmlns:image="http://www.google.com/schemas/sitemap-image/1.1") and/or video (xmlns:video="http://www.google.com/schemas/sitemap-video/1.1") namespace declarations, with <image:image><image:loc> or <video:video> child elements inside <url> entries.
rules.pass_when: The sitemap declares the image and/or video extension namespace and includes at least one <image:image>/<video:video> block describing media metadata; or the site has no significant image/video content to surface.
rules.fail_when: The site relies on image/video search yet the sitemap contains no image:/video: extension elements despite declaring intent to surface media.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the xmlns:image / xmlns:video declaration on <urlset> and one <image:image><image:loc>...</image:loc></image:image> or <video:video> element.

rules.title: URLs are lowercase, hyphenated, descriptive, and shallow
rules.what_to_look_for: The canonical/page URL path segments: lowercase letters, words separated by hyphens (not underscores or spaces/%20), human-readable descriptive slugs, and shallow nesting (few path segments, no deep ID chains or query-string-driven content keys).
rules.pass_when: URL path is all lowercase, uses hyphens to separate words, contains descriptive readable slugs, and is shallow (no excessive depth, no uppercase, no underscores, no encoded spaces).
rules.fail_when: URL path contains uppercase letters, underscores, encoded spaces (%20), non-descriptive IDs/GUIDs as the primary identifier, or excessive depth/parameterization.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the full URL and the canonical <link rel="canonical"> href, highlighting the offending segment (e.g. uppercase or underscore).

rules.title: Redirects use correct status codes and avoid chains
rules.what_to_look_for: Redirect responses: 301/308 for permanent moves, 302/307 for temporary, with a single Location header. Follow the chain and count hops; inspect for loops or mixed/incorrect semantics (e.g. permanent move served as 302).
rules.pass_when: Each redirect returns an appropriate code (301/308 permanent, 302/307 temporary) with a valid Location header, and resolves to the final URL in a single hop (no chain >1 redirect, no loop).
rules.fail_when: A permanent move is served as 302/307 (or vice versa), a redirect chain has 2+ hops, a redirect loop exists, or the Location header is missing/relative-broken.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the status line and Location header for each hop in the chain (e.g. '301 -> /new', '302 -> /final').

rules.title: Not-found pages return real 404/410, not soft 404
rules.what_to_look_for: Request a known-missing URL; compare the HTTP status to the page content. A soft 404 is a page whose body says 'not found'/'page does not exist' (or is empty/error content) yet the response status is 200 OK (or 3xx to a generic page).
rules.pass_when: Requests to nonexistent URLs return HTTP 404 or 410, and pages returning 200 actually contain valid intended content.
rules.fail_when: A page returns HTTP 200 (or redirects to a generic page) while its content indicates not-found/error/empty — the soft-404 anti-pattern.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the requested missing URL, its 200 status line, and the not-found phrasing in the body (e.g. 'Sorry, this page does not exist').

rules.title: Indexing policy explicit and correct via meta robots / X-Robots-Tag
rules.what_to_look_for: The <meta name="robots" content="..."> tag in the HTML head and/or the X-Robots-Tag HTTP response header. Public production pages should be index,follow (or absent = indexable); staging/admin/thin/private pages should carry noindex.
rules.pass_when: Public pages are indexable (no noindex via meta or header) and non-public/thin/staging/admin pages explicitly carry noindex (in <meta name="robots"> or X-Robots-Tag).
rules.fail_when: A public page is unintentionally marked noindex, or a private/staging/admin/thin page is indexable (no noindex directive present in meta tag or X-Robots-Tag header).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <meta name="robots" content="..."> tag and/or the 'X-Robots-Tag:' response header, plus the page's intended visibility.

rules.title: Heading levels form a nested outline without skips
rules.what_to_look_for: The sequence of <h1>-<h6> tags in document order: exactly one top-level <h1>, headings nested in increasing order without skipping a level (no h2 -> h4), and headings used for structure rather than purely for font size/visual styling.
rules.pass_when: Document has a single <h1>, subordinate headings descend without skipping levels (h1->h2->h3), and heading tags convey document structure.
rules.fail_when: No <h1> or multiple <h1>s where one is expected, a heading level is skipped (e.g. <h2> directly to <h4>), or heading tags are used solely for visual styling rather than outline.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the ordered list of heading tags as they appear (e.g. 'h1, h2, h4') marking the skip or the missing/duplicate h1.

rules.title: Pages interlinked with descriptive internal anchors
rules.what_to_look_for: <a href> elements pointing to same-site (relative or same-host) URLs within the main content, with descriptive anchor text (not bare URLs or 'click here'). The page should not be orphaned (zero inbound/outbound internal links).
rules.pass_when: The page contains multiple in-content internal <a href> links to other same-site pages using descriptive anchor text.
rules.fail_when: The page has no in-content internal links (orphan page), or internal links use empty/non-descriptive anchor text like 'click here'/raw URLs only.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote two or three internal descriptive text elements, or note the absence of any in-content internal links.

rules.title: Structured data provided as schema.org JSON-LD
rules.what_to_look_for: <script type="application/ld+json"> blocks in the HTML containing valid JSON with "@context":"https://schema.org" and an "@type" matching the page (Article, Product, Organization, etc.).
rules.pass_when: At least one <script type="application/ld+json"> block is present containing valid JSON with a schema.org @context and an appropriate @type for the page content.
rules.fail_when: No application/ld+json script is present on a page that warrants structured data, or the block contains invalid JSON / missing @context / missing @type.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <script type="application/ld+json"> opening tag and the @context/@type fields of the JSON payload.

rules.title: Breadcrumb trail marked up as BreadcrumbList JSON-LD
rules.what_to_look_for: A visible breadcrumb navigation trail plus a JSON-LD <script type="application/ld+json"> with "@type":"BreadcrumbList" containing ordered itemListElement entries (each with position, name, item).
rules.pass_when: Pages below the top level expose a breadcrumb trail backed by a BreadcrumbList JSON-LD block with ordered itemListElement entries (position/name/item).
rules.fail_when: Deep pages have no breadcrumb trail, or a visible breadcrumb exists with no BreadcrumbList structured data, or the BreadcrumbList lacks ordered itemListElement entries.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the BreadcrumbList JSON-LD @type and its itemListElement positions/names, or note the visible trail without markup.

rules.title: IndexNow configured to notify supporting search engines
rules.what_to_look_for: An IndexNow key file at the site root (e.g. /{key}.txt returning the key as plain text) and/or evidence of IndexNow submissions to Bing/Yandex/Naver/Seznam. Note: IndexNow is not used by Google.
rules.pass_when: An IndexNow key file is reachable at the site root returning the matching key as text/plain (indicating IndexNow is set up), or the site demonstrably submits changed URLs via the IndexNow protocol.
rules.fail_when: No IndexNow key file is present and no IndexNow submission mechanism exists (treated as optional — fail only when IndexNow adoption is expected but absent).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the /{key}.txt URL, its status line, Content-Type, and the key string returned in the body.

rules.title: Text and meaningful non-text meet WCAG contrast ratios
rules.what_to_look_for: Computed foreground vs background colour for text nodes and meaningful UI graphics/icons; compute contrast ratio. Threshold: normal text >=4.5:1, large text (>=24px or >=18.66px bold) >=3:1, meaningful non-text (icons, focus/state indicators, chart elements) >=3:1.
rules.pass_when: Every text node and meaningful non-text element meets its applicable minimum ratio (4.5:1 / 3:1 / 3:1) against its actual rendered background.
rules.fail_when: Any text or meaningful non-text element falls below its threshold, OR text sits on an image/gradient where the effective contrast drops below the minimum in any region.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the element, its foreground/background hex values, and the computed ratio (e.g. '#777 on #fff = 4.48:1, fails 4.5:1'); capture a screenshot of the failing region.

rules.title: Every img has a purpose-appropriate alt attribute
rules.what_to_look_for: Each tag's alt attribute. Informative images need descriptive alt text; purely decorative images need alt="" (empty, present). Also check role="img" elements and for alt/aria-label.
rules.pass_when: Every has an alt attribute: descriptive for informative images, alt="" for decorative ones; image inputs have alt or aria-label.
rules.fail_when: Any is missing the alt attribute entirely, OR an informative image has empty/placeholder alt (e.g. alt="image", filename), OR a decorative image has redundant descriptive alt.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the offending tag including its src and (missing or weak) alt value.

rules.title: Every form control has a programmatically associated label
rules.what_to_look_for: For each <input> (non-hidden), <select>, <textarea>: a <label for="id"> matching its id, a wrapping <label>, or aria-label/aria-labelledby. Confirm placeholder is NOT used as the only label.
rules.pass_when: Every interactive form control has exactly one resolvable accessible name via <label for>, wrapping <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby.
rules.fail_when: Any control has no associated label, relies solely on a placeholder attribute for its name, or has a label whose for does not match any control id.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the control tag and the (absent or placeholder-only) labelling markup, e.g. '<input type=email placeholder="Email"> with no matching <label for>'.

rules.title: All interactive elements are keyboard-operable with no traps
rules.what_to_look_for: Tab/Shift+Tab through the page: every interactive element (links, buttons, inputs, custom widgets, menus, dialogs) receives focus, is operable via Enter/Space/arrows, follows a logical DOM/visual order, and focus can always move away (no trap). Check for positive tabindex values that distort order.
rules.pass_when: Every interactive element is reachable and operable by keyboard, focus order is logical, and focus is never trapped (modal dialogs trap intentionally but release on close/Escape).
rules.fail_when: Any interactive element cannot be focused or activated by keyboard, focus order is illogical, a custom control swallows keys, or focus gets trapped with no keyboard exit.
rules.evidence_hint: Describe the tab sequence and name the element that cannot be reached/activated or where focus is trapped (capture the focus position).

rules.title: Focused elements show a clear visible focus indicator
rules.what_to_look_for: Focus each interactive element and observe the computed :focus / :focus-visible styling. Look for a visible, sufficiently-contrasting (>=3:1 against adjacent colours) outline, border, or background change. Detect outline:none / outline:0 without any replacement indicator.
rules.pass_when: Every focusable element displays a clearly visible focus indicator on keyboard focus with adequate contrast and size.
rules.fail_when: Any element removes the focus indicator (outline:none/0) without providing a visible replacement, or the focus style is invisible/too low-contrast.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the CSS (e.g. ':focus { outline: none; }' with no replacement) and capture before/after-focus screenshots of the element.

rules.title: Skip-to-main-content link is the first focusable element
rules.what_to_look_for:
Near the top of , an anchor like Skip to main content that targets the main content container (matching id or
), appearing as the first focusable element in source order.
rules.pass_when: A skip link is present as (or among) the first focusable elements and targets an existing main-content anchor/id.
rules.fail_when: No skip link exists, OR it is not among the first focusable elements, OR its href target id does not exist on the page.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the skip-link anchor tag and its target element (e.g. '<a href="#main">' -> '<main id="main">').

rules.title: Page uses semantic landmark elements
rules.what_to_look_for: Presence and correct use of landmark elements: <header>, <nav>, <main> (exactly one), <footer>, plus appropriate semantic tags for content (<ul>/<li>, <h1>-<h6>, <article>, <section>) rather than generic <div>/<span> with roles.
rules.pass_when: Document exposes core landmarks (at least one <main>, plus header/nav/footer as appropriate) and uses semantically correct elements for their content roles.
rules.fail_when: No <main>, multiple unlabelled <main>s, missing expected landmarks, or interactive/structural content built from generic <div>/<span> where a native semantic element exists.
rules.evidence_hint: List the landmark elements found (or note their absence) and quote a representative misuse, e.g. '<div class="nav">' used instead of <nav>.

rules.title: Native HTML preferred over redundant or conflicting ARIA
rules.what_to_look_for: ARIA roles/attributes that duplicate native semantics (e.g. role="button" on <button>, role="navigation" on <nav>), or ARIA used to re-create a widget a native element already provides (div with role="checkbox" instead of <input type=checkbox>).
rules.pass_when: Native HTML elements are used for their built-in semantics; ARIA appears only where no native element fits (e.g. complex custom widgets).
rules.fail_when: ARIA roles redundantly restate native element semantics, or ARIA is used to mimic a widget that a native element already provides.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the redundant/conflicting ARIA usage, e.g. '<button role="button">' or '<div role="checkbox">'.

rules.title: Link text describes its destination
rules.what_to_look_for: The accessible name of each <a> (visible text, or aria-label/aria-labelledby). Flag generic phrases: 'click here', 'read more', 'learn more', 'here', 'link', or bare URLs that don't convey destination out of context.
rules.pass_when: Every link's accessible name meaningfully describes its destination or purpose when read out of context.
rules.fail_when: Any link uses non-descriptive text ('click here', 'read more', 'here', etc.) with no supplementing aria-label that clarifies the destination.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the link tag and its text, e.g. 'click here'.

rules.title: No interactive control without an accessible name
rules.what_to_look_for: and ) with no label, or image-only links whose lacks alt.
rules.pass_when: Every link and button has a non-empty accessible name from text, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or labelled child image/icon.
rules.fail_when: Any link or button resolves to an empty accessible name, including icon-only controls with no aria-label and image links whose image has no alt.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the nameless control, e.g. '<button><svg aria-hidden="true"></svg></button>' with no aria-label.

rules.title: Form errors are textual, associated, and announced
rules.what_to_look_for: Error messages presented as text (not colour-only), associated to their input via aria-describedby (or aria-errormessage), invalid fields marked aria-invalid="true", and a live region (role="alert" or aria-live) so errors are announced to assistive tech.
rules.pass_when: Each error is shown as text, tied to its field via aria-describedby/aria-errormessage with aria-invalid, and surfaced in a live region for AT announcement.
rules.fail_when: Errors are colour-only, not programmatically associated with their input, or not announced (no live region / no aria-invalid linkage).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the input and its error markup, e.g. '<input aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="err1"> <span id="err1" role="alert">...'.

rules.title: Primary and inline language declared
rules.what_to_look_for: A valid lang attribute on the root <html> element (e.g. lang="en"), and lang attributes on inline elements containing content in a different language.
rules.pass_when: <html> has a valid lang value matching the primary language, and passages in another language carry their own lang attribute.
rules.fail_when: <html> lacks lang, has an empty/invalid value, or other-language passages have no inline lang attribute.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <html> opening tag with its lang value (or note its absence).

rules.title: prefers-reduced-motion is respected
rules.what_to_look_for: A @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) query that disables/reduces animations, transitions, parallax, and autoplay; verify under simulated reduced-motion that decorative animation/parallax/auto-playing motion stops.
rules.pass_when: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce active, non-essential animation, parallax, and autoplay are disabled or substantially reduced.
rules.fail_when: No prefers-reduced-motion handling exists, OR decorative animation/parallax/autoplay continues to play when reduced motion is requested.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) rule (or note its absence) and capture motion still occurring under the simulated preference.

rules.title: No third-party accessibility overlay widget
rules.what_to_look_for: Script tags or injected widgets from known overlay vendors (e.g. accessiBe/acsbapp, UserWay, AudioEye, EqualWeb, Userway widget div, MaxAccess) that claim runtime WCAG fixing via a floating accessibility button.
rules.pass_when: No third-party accessibility overlay/widget script or its injected toolbar is present.
rules.fail_when: Any overlay vendor script or widget container is present (e.g. acsbapp.com, userway.org, audioeye script, a floating 'accessibility menu' button).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the overlay script tag or widget element, e.g. '<script src="https://acsbapp.com/apps/app/dist/js/app.js">'.

rules.title: Media has captions, transcripts, and audio description
rules.what_to_look_for: For <video>: a <track kind="captions"> (or kind="subtitles") for synchronized captions and ideally kind="descriptions" for audio description; a text transcript link/region for audio and video; embedded players (YouTube/Vimeo iframes) with captions enabled.
rules.pass_when: Video has synchronized captions (<track kind="captions">), audio content has a transcript, and video provides audio description where needed.
rules.fail_when: Video lacks a captions track, audio-only content lacks a transcript, or prerecorded video with meaningful visuals lacks audio description.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <video> element and its <track> tags (or note the missing captions track / transcript).

rules.title: Data tables use real table markup with headers and scope
rules.what_to_look_for: Tabular data rendered as <table> with a <caption>, header cells using <th> (with scope="col"/"row" or headers/id associations), and not faked with <div> grids. Layout tables should not carry data-table semantics.
rules.pass_when: Each data table is a real <table> with <caption>, <th> header cells, and correct scope/headers associations between data and header cells.
rules.fail_when: Tabular data is built from <div>/<span> grids, OR a <table> lacks header <th> cells / scope associations / caption.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the table opening, caption, and a header row (e.g. '<th scope="col">'), or quote the div-grid substitute used instead of <table>.

rules.title: Interactive targets meet minimum size
rules.what_to_look_for: Computed rendered size (including padding/hit area) of interactive controls — buttons, links, form controls, icon buttons. Minimum 24x24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 AA); enhanced target is 44x44 CSS px. Account for spacing exceptions between small targets.
rules.pass_when: Every interactive target is at least 24x24 CSS px (or meets the spacing exception); ideally 44x44 px.
rules.fail_when: Any interactive target renders smaller than 24x24 CSS px without sufficient spacing around it.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the control and its computed dimensions (e.g. 'icon button 18x18px, below 24x24 minimum') and capture the region.

rules.title: Collapsible text uses hidden=until-found
rules.what_to_look_for: Collapsed/accordion content that should remain discoverable: elements using the hidden="until-found" attribute (rather than hidden, display:none, or removal) so find-in-page, AT, and search engines can reach the text.
rules.pass_when: Hidden-but-meaningful collapsible content uses hidden="until-found" so find-in-page and AT can reveal it.
rules.fail_when: Meaningful collapsible text is fully hidden via hidden/display:none/removal in a way that blocks find-in-page and assistive tech, where hidden=until-found would have applied.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the collapsible element's attribute (e.g. 'hidden="until-found"' present, or 'hidden'/style="display:none" used instead).

rules.title: Native interactive elements used over div handlers
rules.what_to_look_for: Generic <div>/<span> carrying click/key handlers (onclick, role + tabindex hacks) where a native element fits: <button>, <a href>, <details>/<summary> for disclosure, <dialog> for modals, <input>/<select> for inputs.
rules.pass_when: Interactive behaviours use the matching native element (button/a/details/summary/dialog/form controls) rather than scripted generic containers.
rules.fail_when: A <div>/<span> with click/key handlers re-implements a control that a native element (<button>, <a>, <details>, <dialog>) provides.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the scripted generic element, e.g. '<div onclick="toggle()">' that should be a <button>.

rules.title: CSS state/relational selectors used over JS class toggling
rules.what_to_look_for: In stylesheets, native state pseudo-classes (:user-invalid, :user-valid, :placeholder-shown, :focus-within) and relational :has() for styling form/validation/UI states, instead of JS toggling classes like .is-invalid/.has-value.
rules.pass_when: Form and UI state styling relies on native CSS pseudo-classes (:user-invalid/:user-valid/:placeholder-shown/:focus-within, optionally via :has()) rather than JS-managed state classes.
rules.fail_when: State styling depends on JavaScript class toggling (e.g. .is-invalid) where native CSS state/relational selectors would suffice.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the relevant CSS (e.g. presence of ':has(:user-invalid)') or the JS toggle / .is-invalid class used in its place.

rules.title: Serve every page over HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or 1.3 and redirect HTTP to HTTPS
rules.what_to_look_for: Negotiated TLS protocol version on the HTTPS connection (must be TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3, not SSLv3/TLS 1.0/TLS 1.1). Request the plain http:// URL and inspect the response status (301/308) and Location header pointing to the https:// equivalent.
rules.pass_when: The page is reachable over https://, the TLS handshake negotiates TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3, and a request to the http:// URL returns a 301/308 redirect whose Location uses the https:// scheme.
rules.fail_when: The page is served over plain http:// without redirect, OR the http:// URL does not redirect to https://, OR the connection negotiates SSLv3/TLS 1.0/TLS 1.1.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the negotiated TLS version (e.g. "TLS 1.3") and the HTTP->HTTPS redirect line (e.g. "HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently" + "Location: https://example.com/").

rules.title: Send Strict-Transport-Security header with max-age, includeSubDomains, and preload
rules.what_to_look_for: The Strict-Transport-Security response header on an HTTPS response. Check for a max-age directive (ideally >= 31536000), the includeSubDomains directive, and the preload directive.
rules.pass_when: Response includes a Strict-Transport-Security header with max-age set to a non-zero value (>= 31536000 recommended), plus includeSubDomains and preload directives.
rules.fail_when: The Strict-Transport-Security header is absent, has max-age=0, or omits includeSubDomains/preload.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the full header line, e.g. "Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload".

rules.title: Define a Content-Security-Policy restricting script, style, image, and frame sources
rules.what_to_look_for: A Content-Security-Policy response header (or a <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"> tag in the HTML). Inspect for explicit directives like default-src, script-src, style-src, img-src, frame-src that name trusted origins rather than relying on a wildcard or 'unsafe-inline'.
rules.pass_when: A Content-Security-Policy is present (header or meta) with a restrictive default-src/script-src that limits sources to trusted origins and does not rely solely on wildcard '*' or 'unsafe-inline' for scripts.
rules.fail_when: No Content-Security-Policy header or meta tag exists, OR the policy uses script-src '*' / 'unsafe-inline' with no other restriction (effectively no XSS protection).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the Content-Security-Policy header value or the <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="..."> tag.

rules.title: Publish a /.well-known/security.txt vulnerability disclosure file
rules.what_to_look_for: Fetch https://<domain>/.well-known/security.txt and check the response is HTTP 200 with a body containing at least a Contact: field (RFC 9116). An Expires: field is also expected.
rules.pass_when: Requesting /.well-known/security.txt returns HTTP 200 and the body contains a Contact: line (e.g. a mailto: or https: URL).
rules.fail_when: /.well-known/security.txt returns 404/non-200, or the file exists but has no Contact: field.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the response status and the Contact: line (and Expires: line if present) from the security.txt body.

rules.title: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
rules.what_to_look_for: The X-Content-Type-Options response header and its exact value, which must be the token nosniff.
rules.pass_when: Response includes the header X-Content-Type-Options with value exactly nosniff.
rules.fail_when: The X-Content-Type-Options header is absent or set to any value other than nosniff.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the header line "X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff".

rules.title: Restrict framing via CSP frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options
rules.what_to_look_for: A Content-Security-Policy header containing a frame-ancestors directive (preferred), and/or a legacy X-Frame-Options header. Check the values restrict embedding to 'self', 'none', or a named allow-list rather than permitting any origin.
rules.pass_when: Response carries CSP frame-ancestors limiting framers to 'none'/'self'/specific origins, OR an X-Frame-Options header set to DENY or SAMEORIGIN.
rules.fail_when: Neither CSP frame-ancestors nor X-Frame-Options is present, OR frame-ancestors is set to a permissive wildcard '*' allowing any site to iframe the page.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the frame-ancestors directive from the CSP header and/or the "X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN" line.

rules.title: Send a Referrer-Policy header (strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter)
rules.what_to_look_for: The Referrer-Policy response header (or <meta name="referrer">). Check its value is a privacy-preserving policy such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin, strict-origin, no-referrer, or same-origin.
rules.pass_when: A Referrer-Policy header (or meta) is present with a value of strict-origin-when-cross-origin or a stricter policy (strict-origin, same-origin, no-referrer).
rules.fail_when: No Referrer-Policy is set, OR it is set to a leaky value such as unsafe-url or no-referrer-when-downgrade.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the header line, e.g. "Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin".

rules.title: Send a Permissions-Policy disabling unused powerful features
rules.what_to_look_for: The Permissions-Policy response header. Check that high-risk features the site does not use — camera, microphone, geolocation, payment, usb — are disabled, e.g. camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=().
rules.pass_when: A Permissions-Policy header is present and sets the unused powerful features (camera, microphone, geolocation, payment, usb) to an empty allow-list () or self-only.
rules.fail_when: No Permissions-Policy header is present, OR it leaves powerful features open to all origins (e.g. camera=*) without restriction.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the header line, e.g. "Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=()".

rules.title: Add Subresource Integrity hashes to third-party scripts and stylesheets
rules.what_to_look_for: In the raw HTML, every <script src> and <link rel="stylesheet" href> pointing to a cross-origin/CDN host. Each such element should carry an integrity="sha256-...|sha384-...|sha512-..." attribute plus crossorigin="anonymous".
rules.pass_when: All cross-origin <script> and stylesheet <link> elements include a valid integrity attribute (sha256/384/512 hash) together with crossorigin.
rules.fail_when: One or more cross-origin third-party <script src> or <link rel=stylesheet> elements lack an integrity attribute.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote an offending or compliant tag, e.g. "<script src=\"https://cdn.example.com/lib.js\" integrity=\"sha384-...\" crossorigin=\"anonymous\">".

rules.title: Set Secure, HttpOnly, and explicit SameSite on cookies with __Host-/__Secure- prefixes for session cookies
rules.what_to_look_for: Each Set-Cookie response header. Check for the Secure and HttpOnly attributes and an explicit SameSite=Lax|Strict|None value. For session/auth cookies, check the cookie name uses a __Host- or __Secure- prefix.
rules.pass_when: Every Set-Cookie carries Secure, HttpOnly, and an explicit SameSite attribute, and session cookies use a __Host- or __Secure- name prefix.
rules.fail_when: Any cookie is missing Secure or HttpOnly, lacks an explicit SameSite, uses SameSite=None without Secure, or a session cookie omits the __Host-/__Secure- prefix.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote a Set-Cookie line, e.g. "Set-Cookie: __Host-session=abc; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/".

rules.title: Publish DNS CAA records restricting which CAs may issue certificates
rules.what_to_look_for: Query DNS-over-HTTPS: WebFetch `https://dns.google/resolve?name=<domain>&type=CAA`. In the returned JSON `Answer` array, look for CAA records (type 257) whose data contains `issue` / `issuewild` property tags naming authorized CAs, optionally an `iodef` tag.
rules.pass_when: The domain returns at least one CAA record with an issue (and/or issuewild) tag naming the permitted CA(s).
rules.fail_when: No CAA records exist for the domain (any publicly trusted CA may issue certificates).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the CAA record(s), e.g. "example.com. CAA 0 issue \"letsencrypt.org\"".

rules.title: Enable DNSSEC signing for the domain
rules.what_to_look_for: Query DNS-over-HTTPS: WebFetch `https://dns.google/resolve?name=<domain>&type=A` (or any type). In the returned JSON, read the top-level `AD` flag (Authenticated Data) — `AD:true` means a validating resolver confirmed the DNSSEC chain of trust. Optionally also query type=DNSKEY/DS to see signing records.
rules.pass_when: The domain publishes DNSKEY and RRSIG records, a matching DS record exists in the parent zone, and the DNSSEC chain validates.
rules.fail_when: No DS/DNSKEY records exist, or the DNSSEC chain fails to validate (zone is unsigned or bogus).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the DS record at the parent and/or DNSKEY/RRSIG presence and the validating resolver's AD (Authenticated Data) flag.

rules.title: /.well-known/ path serves standardized metadata (RFC 8615)
rules.what_to_look_for: Issue GET requests to one or more standardized /.well-known/<suffix> URIs registered per RFC 8615 (e.g. /.well-known/security.txt, /.well-known/change-password). Inspect HTTP status and that the path is served from the origin root, not rewritten into a SPA catch-all. A 200 with a resource-appropriate Content-Type confirms the well-known mechanism is wired up.
rules.pass_when: At least one registered /.well-known/<suffix> URI returns HTTP 200 (or a valid 3xx redirect for redirect-style endpoints) with a Content-Type matching the resource type, served from the domain root.
rules.fail_when: Every probed /.well-known/<suffix> returns 404, or the server returns the SPA index.html (HTML Content-Type with the app shell) for these paths instead of the resource, indicating no well-known support.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the request URL, the HTTP status line, and the Content-Type header of the well-known response.

rules.title: /.well-known/change-password redirects to change-password page
rules.what_to_look_for: GET /.well-known/change-password and inspect the response status and Location header. This endpoint should be a redirect (301/302/303/307/308) whose Location points to the real change-password page (e.g. /settings/password, /account/security). Only applicable if the site has user accounts.
rules.pass_when: Site has no accounts (rule N/A), OR /.well-known/change-password returns a 3xx redirect with a Location header pointing to a working change-password page.
rules.fail_when: Site has user accounts but /.well-known/change-password returns 404, returns 200 with the app shell instead of a redirect, or redirects to a non-existent/unrelated page.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the HTTP status line and the Location header value of the /.well-known/change-password response.

rules.title: /.well-known/openid-configuration exposes valid OIDC discovery JSON
rules.what_to_look_for: GET /.well-known/openid-configuration. Inspect status, Content-Type (should be application/json), and that the JSON body contains required OIDC discovery fields: issuer, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, jwks_uri. Only applicable if the site is itself an OIDC identity provider.
rules.pass_when: Site is not an OIDC IdP (rule N/A), OR the endpoint returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and a body containing at least issuer, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, and jwks_uri.
rules.fail_when: Site advertises being an OIDC IdP but the endpoint returns 404, non-JSON content, or JSON missing one of the required discovery fields (issuer/authorization_endpoint/token_endpoint/jwks_uri).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the HTTP status, the Content-Type header, and the issuer + endpoint keys from the JSON body.

rules.title: /.well-known/api-catalog returns RFC 9727 Linkset API index
rules.what_to_look_for: GET /.well-known/api-catalog and inspect status and Content-Type. Per RFC 9727 it should return a Linkset document: Content-Type application/linkset+json (or application/linkset) whose body contains a linkset array of link objects with anchor and href entries pointing to the site's APIs.
rules.pass_when: The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/linkset+json or application/linkset and a body containing a linkset structure with at least one link to an API resource.
rules.fail_when: The endpoint returns 404, returns 200 but with a non-linkset Content-Type (e.g. text/html app shell or plain application/json without linkset structure), or an empty/malformed linkset.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the HTTP status, the Content-Type header, and the linkset array (or its first link object with anchor/href) from the body.

rules.title: /.well-known/webfinger resolves acct: identifiers (RFC 7033)
rules.what_to_look_for: GET /.well-known/webfinger?resource=acct:user@domain for a known account. Inspect status and Content-Type (application/jrd+json). The JRD body should contain a subject matching the queried resource and a links array. Only applicable to Fediverse / federated-identity sites.
rules.pass_when: Site is not federated (rule N/A), OR a webfinger query with a valid resource parameter returns HTTP 200, Content-Type application/jrd+json, and a JRD body with a matching subject and a links array.
rules.fail_when: Site participates in the Fediverse but /.well-known/webfinger returns 404 for a valid acct: resource, ignores the resource parameter, or returns a body lacking subject/links.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the request URL with the resource parameter, the HTTP status, the Content-Type header, and the subject + links fields from the JRD body.

rules.title: /.well-known/apple-app-site-association declares Universal Links
rules.what_to_look_for: GET /.well-known/apple-app-site-association. Inspect status and that the body is valid JSON served WITHOUT a redirect and with Content-Type application/json (Apple requires no redirects). The JSON should contain an applinks object with appIDs/components (or details) mapping Apple app IDs to handled URL paths.
rules.pass_when: Site has no associated iOS app (rule N/A), OR the endpoint returns HTTP 200 directly (no redirect) with valid JSON containing an applinks section listing app IDs and URL components.
rules.fail_when: An iOS app is associated but the endpoint 404s, is served via a redirect, has a non-application/json or HTML Content-Type, or the JSON lacks a valid applinks structure.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the HTTP status (confirming no redirect), the Content-Type header, and the applinks/appIDs portion of the JSON body.

rules.title: /.well-known/assetlinks.json declares Android App Links
rules.what_to_look_for: GET /.well-known/assetlinks.json. Inspect status and Content-Type (application/json). The body should be a JSON array of Digital Asset Links statements, each with a relation array (e.g. delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls) and a target object containing namespace=android_app, package_name, and sha256_cert_fingerprints.
rules.pass_when: Site has no associated Android app (rule N/A), OR the endpoint returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and a JSON array of statements each containing relation plus a target with package_name and sha256_cert_fingerprints.
rules.fail_when: An Android app is associated but the endpoint 404s, returns non-JSON/HTML content, or returns statements missing relation, package_name, or sha256_cert_fingerprints.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the HTTP status, the Content-Type header, and the first statement's relation + target.package_name + sha256_cert_fingerprints from the body.

rules.title: /.well-known/nodeinfo links to NodeInfo discovery document
rules.what_to_look_for: GET /.well-known/nodeinfo. Inspect status and Content-Type (application/json). The body should contain a links array with rel values referencing a NodeInfo schema (e.g. http://nodeinfo.diaspora.software/ns/schema/2.x) and an href pointing to the actual NodeInfo JSON document. Only applicable to federated platforms.
rules.pass_when: Site is not a federated platform (rule N/A), OR the endpoint returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and a links array whose entries carry a NodeInfo schema rel and a resolvable href.
rules.fail_when: Site is a federated platform but /.well-known/nodeinfo returns 404, returns non-JSON content, or returns a body lacking a links array with a NodeInfo schema rel/href.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the HTTP status, the Content-Type header, and the links[].rel + links[].href entries from the body.

rules.title: /.well-known/traffic-advice instructs private prefetch proxies
rules.what_to_look_for: GET /.well-known/traffic-advice. Inspect status and Content-Type, which must be application/trafficadvice+json. The body should be a JSON array of advice objects, each with a user_agent field (e.g. "prefetch-proxy") and a fraction (0.0-1.0) indicating allowed prefetch volume.
rules.pass_when: The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/trafficadvice+json and a JSON array of objects each containing user_agent and a numeric fraction between 0.0 and 1.0.
rules.fail_when: The endpoint 404s, returns a Content-Type other than application/trafficadvice+json, or returns a body that is not a JSON array of {user_agent, fraction} objects.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the HTTP status, the Content-Type header, and the first advice object's user_agent + fraction from the body.

rules.title: Core agent-readiness signals present
rules.what_to_look_for: Aggregate baseline: canonical <link rel="canonical"> with a stable absolute URL, at least one <script type="application/ld+json"> JSON-LD block, semantic landmark elements (<main>, <article>, <nav>, <header>), and a reachable /robots.txt. Inspect the raw HTML <head> and document outline plus the site root for robots.txt.
rules.pass_when: The page exposes a stable canonical URL, semantic HTML5 landmarks, at least one JSON-LD block, and robots.txt is reachable at the root.
rules.fail_when: No canonical URL, no semantic landmarks, no structured data, AND no robots.txt — i.e. the page offers no machine-affordances beyond raw HTML.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <link rel="canonical"> href, the opening <main>/<article> tags, the first JSON-LD <script> snippet, and the robots.txt HTTP status.

rules.title: /llms.txt index present at root
rules.what_to_look_for: GET {origin}/llms.txt — inspect the response status and Content-Type. Body should be Markdown beginning with an H1 (# Title) followed by link lists per the llms.txt spec.
rules.pass_when: GET /llms.txt returns HTTP 200 with a text/markdown or text/plain body that starts with a Markdown H1 heading.
rules.fail_when: GET /llms.txt returns 404 / non-2xx, or returns HTML instead of Markdown content.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the /llms.txt HTTP status line, Content-Type header, and the first H1 line of the body.

rules.title: /llms-full.txt concatenated content present at root
rules.what_to_look_for: GET {origin}/llms-full.txt — inspect response status and Content-Type. Body should be the concatenated full Markdown of key pages (substantially larger than llms.txt).
rules.pass_when: GET /llms-full.txt returns HTTP 200 with a Markdown/plain-text body containing concatenated page content.
rules.fail_when: GET /llms-full.txt returns 404 / non-2xx, or returns HTML rather than concatenated Markdown.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the /llms-full.txt HTTP status, Content-Type, and Content-Length (or first/last lines showing concatenated sections).

rules.title: Per-page Markdown source endpoint available
rules.what_to_look_for: Append .md to the current page URL (e.g. /page -> /page.md) OR re-request the page with Accept: text/markdown. Inspect status and Content-Type of the response.
rules.pass_when: The .md-suffixed URL or content-negotiated request returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/markdown (or text/plain Markdown) mirroring the page content.
rules.fail_when: The .md URL returns 404 / non-2xx AND Accept: text/markdown content negotiation returns HTML.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the requested URL or Accept header, the response status, and the Content-Type header proving Markdown was served.

rules.title: robots.txt declares AI crawler user-agents
rules.what_to_look_for: GET {origin}/robots.txt and scan for User-agent lines naming AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot, CCBot, Bytespider, etc.) each paired with an explicit Allow: or Disallow: directive.
rules.pass_when: robots.txt contains at least one AI-crawler User-agent block with an explicit Allow or Disallow rule.
rules.fail_when: robots.txt is missing, or contains only a generic User-agent: * with no AI-specific user-agent group.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the matching User-agent line(s) and their Allow/Disallow directives from robots.txt.

rules.title: Content-Signal directives present in robots.txt
rules.what_to_look_for: GET {origin}/robots.txt and scan for Content-Signal: directives expressing search / ai-input / ai-train permissions (e.g. Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-train=no), per the Content Signals proposal.
rules.pass_when: robots.txt contains at least one Content-Signal directive specifying search/ingest/train preferences.
rules.fail_when: robots.txt contains no Content-Signal directive.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the Content-Signal line(s) from robots.txt.

rules.title: Web Bot Auth request signing supported
rules.what_to_look_for: Evidence the site advertises/accepts RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures for bot identity: a Signature-Agent response header, a published signature-agent directory, or a /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory endpoint listing the bot's verification keys.
rules.pass_when: The site exposes a signature-agent key directory or documents acceptance of RFC 9421 Signature/Signature-Input headers for bot authentication.
rules.fail_when: No signature-agent directory, no RFC 9421 signing affordance, and no Web Bot Auth documentation/headers are present.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the Signature-Agent header or the /.well-known signature directory response and its key entries.

rules.title: Published URLs remain stable and resolvable
rules.what_to_look_for: Request the page's canonical/published URL directly. Inspect the status and any redirect chain. A stable URL returns the content at the published URL without 404, 410, or a redirect to an unrelated/temporary location.
rules.pass_when: The published URL returns HTTP 200 directly (or a single 301 to a documented canonical), serving the intended content with no broken link.
rules.fail_when: The published URL returns 404/410, or a soft-404, or redirects to an unrelated page — breaking citations, bookmarks, and caches.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the requested URL, the final HTTP status, and the full redirect chain (Location headers) if any.

rules.title: JSON-LD schema.org structured data present
rules.what_to_look_for: In the raw HTML, find <script type="application/ld+json"> blocks whose JSON parses and contains an @context of schema.org and a recognized @type (e.g. Article, Product, Organization, FAQPage).
rules.pass_when: At least one valid <script type="application/ld+json"> block parses as JSON with a schema.org @context and a typed @type expressing page facts.
rules.fail_when: No JSON-LD script block exists, or the block fails to parse / lacks @context and @type.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the JSON-LD <script> block showing @context and @type.

rules.title: Machine-readable alternate formats offered
rules.what_to_look_for: In the HTML <head>, look for <link rel="alternate"> entries with type application/json, application/rss+xml, application/feed+json, or text/markdown advertising a JSON/RSS/Markdown representation of the content alongside the HTML.
rules.pass_when: At least one <link rel="alternate"> (or documented endpoint) advertises a JSON, RSS/Atom, or Markdown representation of the page content.
rules.fail_when: Only HTML is offered; no alternate JSON/RSS/Markdown link or endpoint is advertised.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <link rel="alternate"> tag(s) with their type and href attributes.

rules.title: HTTP Link header advertises discovery resources
rules.what_to_look_for: Inspect the response Link: header for rel values advertising agent resources, e.g. rel="llms.txt", rel="sitemap", rel="api-catalog", or rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml".
rules.pass_when: The Link response header contains at least one rel pointing to llms.txt, sitemap, api-catalog, or an RSS/feed resource.
rules.fail_when: No Link header is present, or it carries no discovery-related rel values.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the full Link: response header line(s) and the relevant rel attribute.

rules.title: MCP tool endpoint discoverable
rules.what_to_look_for: Evidence of a Model Context Protocol endpoint: a documented JSON-RPC MCP URL (e.g. /mcp) that responds to a tools/list JSON-RPC request, or an advertised link/well-known entry pointing to an MCP server.
rules.pass_when: An MCP endpoint is advertised and responds to a JSON-RPC tools/list (or initialize) request with a valid MCP result.
rules.fail_when: No MCP endpoint is advertised or reachable, and no JSON-RPC tool interface responds.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the MCP endpoint URL and the JSON-RPC tools/list response showing exposed tool names.

rules.title: A2A agent card published at well-known URI
rules.what_to_look_for: GET {origin}/.well-known/agent-card.json — inspect status and body. Expect JSON describing an A2A agent (name, capabilities, JSON-RPC endpoint URL) per the Agent-to-Agent spec.
rules.pass_when: GET /.well-known/agent-card.json returns HTTP 200 with valid JSON containing A2A agent metadata (name + service endpoint).
rules.fail_when: GET /.well-known/agent-card.json returns 404 / non-2xx or non-JSON content.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the /.well-known/agent-card.json HTTP status and the JSON fields (name, url/endpoint, capabilities).

rules.title: Agent Skills listed at well-known URI
rules.what_to_look_for: GET the Agent Skills well-known URI (e.g. /.well-known/agent-skills or the path named in the Cloudflare-led draft RFC) — inspect status and body for a JSON/manifest listing available Agent Skills.
rules.pass_when: The Agent Skills well-known URI returns HTTP 200 with a manifest enumerating one or more Agent Skills.
rules.fail_when: The Agent Skills well-known URI returns 404 / non-2xx or contains no skills listing.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the well-known URI requested, its HTTP status, and the skills-listing JSON entries.

rules.title: DNS-AID SVCB/HTTPS records published
rules.what_to_look_for: Query DNS-over-HTTPS: WebFetch `https://dns.google/resolve?name=_agents.<domain>&type=HTTPS` (and `&type=SVCB`). In the returned JSON `Answer` array, look for SVCB/HTTPS records advertising agent service endpoints (DNS for AI Discovery).
rules.pass_when: A DNS query for _agents.<domain> returns at least one SVCB or HTTPS record pointing to an agent service.
rules.fail_when: No SVCB/HTTPS record exists under _agents.<domain> (NXDOMAIN or empty answer).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the dig/DNS answer section showing the SVCB/HTTPS record for _agents.<domain>.

rules.title: NLWeb conversational endpoint advertised
rules.what_to_look_for: In the HTML <head>, look for <link rel="nlweb"> pointing to an NLWeb endpoint, and/or a reachable NLWeb endpoint that answers natural-language queries via MCP JSON-RPC.
rules.pass_when: A <link rel="nlweb"> is present (and/or the referenced endpoint responds), advertising a conversational NLWeb interface.
rules.fail_when: No rel="nlweb" link is present and no NLWeb endpoint is advertised.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <link rel="nlweb"> tag with its href, and the endpoint response if probed.

rules.title: WebMCP navigator.modelContext tools registered
rules.what_to_look_for: In a live browser, after page load check window.navigator.modelContext and whether the page registers in-browser tools via the WebMCP navigator.modelContext JS API (e.g. registerTool / provideContext calls).
rules.pass_when: navigator.modelContext exists and the page registers at least one in-browser tool through the WebMCP API.
rules.fail_when: navigator.modelContext is undefined or no tools are registered via the WebMCP API.
rules.evidence_hint: Capture the evaluated navigator.modelContext object and the list of registered tool names from the live page.

rules.title: /schemamap.xml index present at root
rules.what_to_look_for: GET {origin}/schemamap.xml — inspect status and body. Expect XML indexing one JSON-LD endpoint per resource type per the Schemamap spec.
rules.pass_when: GET /schemamap.xml returns HTTP 200 with XML listing per-resource JSON-LD endpoint URLs.
rules.fail_when: GET /schemamap.xml returns 404 / non-2xx or non-XML content.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the /schemamap.xml HTTP status and the XML entries mapping resources to JSON-LD endpoints.

rules.title: Core Web Vitals LCP/INP/CLS within thresholds
rules.what_to_look_for: Measure field/lab Core Web Vitals on a live page load: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) via the web-vitals library, PerformanceObserver, or a Lighthouse/CrUX run at the 75th percentile.
rules.pass_when: LCP <= 2.5s AND INP <= 200ms AND CLS <= 0.1 at the 75th percentile.
rules.fail_when: Any of LCP > 2.5s, INP > 200ms, or CLS > 0.1 at the 75th percentile.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the three measured metric values (e.g. 'LCP 1.9s, INP 140ms, CLS 0.04') and the measurement source (Lighthouse/CrUX/web-vitals).

rules.title: Images use modern formats and explicit dimensions
rules.what_to_look_for: and / elements: src/srcset pointing to .webp or .avif (or type="image/webp"/"image/avif"), explicit width and height attributes (or aspect-ratio), and srcset/sizes for responsive selection per viewport.
rules.pass_when: Content images are served as WebP/AVIF (with fallback), carry explicit width+height (or aspect-ratio), and use srcset/sizes for viewport-appropriate sizing.
rules.fail_when: Images are only JPEG/PNG with no WebP/AVIF source, OR lack width/height (or aspect-ratio), OR ship a single oversized asset with no srcset/sizes.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote an / tag showing format, width/height, and srcset/sizes (or one missing them).

rules.title: Off-screen media lazy-loaded, LCP element eager
rules.what_to_look_for: loading="lazy" on off-screen ,
rules.pass_when: Off-screen images/iframes/videos carry loading="lazy" AND the LCP/above-fold hero element does NOT carry loading="lazy".
rules.fail_when: Off-screen media omits loading="lazy", OR the LCP/hero element has loading="lazy" applied to it.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote an off-screen and the hero tag showing its loading attribute.

rules.title: Critical resources preloaded, third-party preconnected
rules.what_to_look_for: In <head>: <link rel="preload"> for the LCP image and critical fonts (with as= and crossorigin for fonts), <link rel="preconnect"> for third-party origins, and <link rel="prefetch"> for likely-next-navigation resources.
rules.pass_when: Head contains rel="preload" for the LCP image and/or critical fonts and rel="preconnect" for third-party origins used early.
rules.fail_when: No preload for the LCP image/critical fonts and no preconnect for third-party origins, despite such resources being present.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <link rel="preload">/<link rel="preconnect"> tags found in <head>.

rules.title: Cache-Control immutable for assets, short for HTML
rules.what_to_look_for: Cache-Control response header on fingerprinted static assets (hashed filenames) vs on HTML documents: 'immutable, max-age=31536000' for assets, and 'no-cache' / short max-age / must-revalidate for HTML.
rules.pass_when: Fingerprinted assets return Cache-Control with max-age=31536000 and immutable, AND HTML documents return no-cache or a short max-age.
rules.fail_when: Fingerprinted assets lack long max-age/immutable, OR HTML is served with a long/immutable cache lifetime.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the Cache-Control header line from a hashed asset response and from the HTML document response.

rules.title: No-Vary-Search declares non-varying query params
rules.what_to_look_for: No-Vary-Search response header on responses whose query parameters do not change the body (e.g. 'params, except=("q")' or 'key-order, params=("utm_source")').
rules.pass_when: Responses that ignore certain query params for content send a No-Vary-Search header declaring those params.
rules.fail_when: No No-Vary-Search header is present where query-param-insensitive responses exist (cache/prefetch cannot dedupe variants).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the No-Vary-Search header line, or note its absence on a query-param-insensitive endpoint.

rules.title: Text responses compressed with brotli/gzip
rules.what_to_look_for: Content-Encoding response header (br, zstd, or gzip) on text assets (HTML/CSS/JS/JSON/SVG) when the request sends Accept-Encoding; and the absence of compression on already-compressed media (jpg/png/webp/mp4/woff2).
rules.pass_when: Text/HTML/CSS/JS responses carry Content-Encoding: br (or zstd) where supported and gzip otherwise; media is not re-compressed.
rules.fail_when: Text assets are served with no Content-Encoding, OR media binaries are double-compressed.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the Content-Encoding header line on a CSS/JS response and the request Accept-Encoding.

rules.title: Fonts self-hosted WOFF2, subset, font-display swap
rules.what_to_look_for: @font-face rules (or linked CSS) using src .woff2 from a same-origin path, font-display: swap (or optional/fallback), subset character ranges (unicode-range), and <link rel="preload" as="font" crossorigin> for the critical face.
rules.pass_when: Fonts are self-hosted WOFF2 with font-display: swap and the critical face is preloaded with crossorigin.
rules.fail_when: Fonts load from a third-party origin without preconnect/preload, OR lack font-display (blocking render), OR are not WOFF2.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the @font-face src/font-display declaration and any <link rel="preload" as="font"> tag.

rules.title: Above-fold CSS inlined, rest deferred non-blocking
rules.what_to_look_for: An inline <style> block in <head> with critical above-the-fold CSS, and non-critical stylesheets loaded non-blockingly (rel="preload" as="style" onload swap, media trick, or below-fold injection) rather than plain render-blocking <link rel="stylesheet"> in head.
rules.pass_when: Critical CSS is inlined in <head> AND non-critical CSS is loaded without blocking render.
rules.fail_when: All CSS arrives via render-blocking <link rel="stylesheet"> in <head> with no inlined critical CSS.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the inline <style> in head and the non-blocking <link> loading pattern (or the blocking <link> that fails).

rules.title: Scripts use defer/async/module, not blocking head
rules.what_to_look_for: <script> tags: defer on first-party app code, async on independent third-party scripts, type="module" for modern code; and the absence of bare blocking <script src> in <head> without defer/async/module.
rules.pass_when: App scripts use defer, third-party scripts use async, modern scripts use type="module"; no render-blocking bare <script src> sits in <head>.
rules.fail_when: A synchronous <script src> without defer/async/module appears in <head>, blocking parsing.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <script> tags showing defer/async/type=module, or the blocking head <script> that fails.

rules.title: Served over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3
rules.what_to_look_for: Negotiated protocol version of the main document/asset responses (HTTP/2 'h2' or HTTP/3 'h3'); presence of an Alt-Svc header advertising h3 for HTTP/3 upgrade.
rules.pass_when: Responses are served over HTTP/2 (h2) at minimum, with HTTP/3 (h3, advertised via Alt-Svc) where available.
rules.fail_when: Responses are served only over HTTP/1.1.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the negotiated protocol (e.g. 'HTTP/2 200') and any Alt-Svc: h3 header.

rules.title: Speculation Rules prefetch/prerender configured
rules.what_to_look_for: A <script type="speculationrules"> block (inline JSON) or Speculation-Rules response header declaring prefetch and/or prerender rules with source/where/eagerness for likely next navigations.
rules.pass_when: A valid speculationrules script (or Speculation-Rules header) declares prefetch/prerender for next-navigation links.
rules.fail_when: No Speculation Rules are present despite predictable next-navigation links.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <script type="speculationrules"> JSON or the Speculation-Rules header.

rules.title: Resource hints used for early connections/fetches
rules.what_to_look_for: <link> resource hints in <head>: rel="dns-prefetch", rel="preconnect", rel="preload", rel="modulepreload", and rel="prefetch" each pointing at the appropriate origin/resource with correct as=/crossorigin attributes.
rules.pass_when: Appropriate resource hints (dns-prefetch/preconnect/preload/modulepreload/prefetch) are present for cross-origin connections and critical/next resources.
rules.fail_when: No resource hints are present despite cross-origin dependencies or module/critical resources that would benefit.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the rel= resource-hint <link> tags found in <head>.

rules.title: View Transitions opted in (same/cross-doc)
rules.what_to_look_for: CSS '@view-transition { navigation: auto; }' for cross-document transitions, view-transition-name declarations on elements, and/or JS document.startViewTransition() usage for same-document transitions.
rules.pass_when: The page opts into View Transitions via @view-transition (cross-doc) or document.startViewTransition()/view-transition-name (same-doc).
rules.fail_when: No View Transitions opt-in is present on a navigation/SPA flow that would benefit.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the @view-transition rule, view-transition-name declaration, or startViewTransition() call.

rules.title: Pages remain BFCache-eligible
rules.what_to_look_for: Back/forward cache eligibility on navigation: no 'unload' event listeners, no Cache-Control: no-store on the document, properly closed connections; verify via the pageshow event's persisted flag or Chrome DevTools BFCache tester after a back/forward navigation.
rules.pass_when: After a back/forward navigation the page is restored from BFCache (pageshow event.persisted === true) with no disqualifying conditions.
rules.fail_when: The page is excluded from BFCache (e.g. due to unload handlers or Cache-Control: no-store), forcing a full reload.
rules.evidence_hint: Capture the DevTools BFCache test result or pageshow.persisted value, and any no-store header / unload listener found.

rules.title: Off-screen content uses content-visibility/IO
rules.what_to_look_for: CSS 'content-visibility: auto' paired with 'contain-intrinsic-size' on long/off-screen sections, and/or IntersectionObserver usage in JS to defer rendering/work for off-screen content.
rules.pass_when: Long off-screen sections use content-visibility: auto with contain-intrinsic-size, and/or IntersectionObserver defers off-screen work.
rules.fail_when: Long off-screen content is fully rendered eagerly with no content-visibility or IntersectionObserver deferral.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the content-visibility/contain-intrinsic-size CSS or the IntersectionObserver instantiation.

rules.title: CSS containment applied to independent subtrees
rules.what_to_look_for: CSS 'contain' property declarations: contain: layout, contain: paint, contain: style (or shorthand like contain: content/strict) on independent UI components/widgets.
rules.pass_when: Independent component subtrees declare contain: layout/paint/style to scope layout and paint work.
rules.fail_when: No contain declarations exist on components that would benefit (purely optional — failure is informational).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the CSS rule containing the contain: declaration.

rules.title: Animations driven by scroll/view timelines
rules.what_to_look_for: CSS scroll-driven animation primitives: 'animation-timeline: scroll()' / 'view()', or named scroll-timeline / view-timeline declarations tied to an animation, rather than JS scroll-event-driven animation loops.
rules.pass_when: Scroll-linked animations use scroll-timeline/view-timeline (animation-timeline: scroll()/view()) instead of main-thread scroll handlers.
rules.fail_when: No scroll-driven CSS timelines are used where scroll-linked animations exist (purely optional — failure is informational).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the animation-timeline / scroll-timeline / view-timeline CSS declaration.

rules.title: scrollbar-gutter:stable reserves scrollbar space
rules.what_to_look_for: CSS 'scrollbar-gutter: stable' (or 'stable both-edges') on the root/html or a scroll container, reserving gutter space so appearing scrollbars do not shift layout.
rules.pass_when: scrollbar-gutter: stable is declared on the relevant scroll container/root to prevent scrollbar-induced layout shift.
rules.fail_when: No scrollbar-gutter: stable is set where overlay/classic scrollbar appearance would cause horizontal layout shift.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the CSS rule containing scrollbar-gutter: stable.

rules.title: Linked privacy policy page covering required disclosures
rules.what_to_look_for: An anchor in the page source linking to a privacy policy: an <a> whose href points to a path/URL containing 'privacy' (e.g. /privacy, /privacy-policy, /legal/privacy) or whose visible link text matches /privacy\s*policy/i, typically in the footer. Then fetch that page and look for sections naming: what data is collected, purpose/why, legal basis, third-party sharing, retention period, and user rights (access/erasure/objection).
rules.pass_when: A reachable privacy-policy link exists (href returns 2xx) AND the linked document contains text addressing all six disclosures: data collected, purpose, legal basis, sharing, retention, and user rights.
rules.fail_when: No privacy-policy link is present in the HTML, the link 404s/is unreachable, or the linked document omits one or more required disclosures (e.g. no legal basis or no retention statement).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the footer Privacy Policy tag and the section headings/sentences in the policy that cover each of the six disclosures.

rules.title: Opt-in cookie consent gate before non-essential cookies
rules.what_to_look_for: In raw HTML, a consent management banner/script before any non-essential trackers fire: CMP markers such as elements with id/class containing 'cookie-consent', 'cookie-banner', 'cmp', or known CMP scripts (e.g. cookiebot 'Cookiebot', OneTrust 'otSDKStub'/'optanon', Osano, Usercentrics, Klaro, CookieYes). Non-essential tags (analytics/marketing: Google Analytics gtag/ga, Facebook Pixel 'fbq', etc.) must be present only as type="text/plain" with a data-* category attribute (consent-gated) rather than directly executable, OR absent until consent.
rules.pass_when: A CMP/consent banner is present AND non-essential tracking scripts are blocked pending opt-in (loaded as type="text/plain"/data-cookieconsent-style attributes, or not emitted before consent).
rules.fail_when: Non-essential cookies/trackers (analytics, ads, pixels) load unconditionally on first paint with no consent mechanism, or a banner exists but is opt-out only (scripts fire before any user action).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the CMP banner element/script tag and any non-essential <script> showing whether it is consent-gated (type="text/plain" data-category) or fires immediately.

rules.title: Global Privacy Control signal honored
rules.what_to_look_for: With a browser exposing navigator.globalPrivacyControl=true (GPC signal sent), inspect the CMP/consent state and network: the site should auto-apply an opt-out — e.g. CMP API (OneTrust, Cookiebot) reflects opted-out categories, a consent cookie records 'do not sell/share', and non-essential/advertising requests are suppressed. Also check the privacy policy/site text for an explicit statement that GPC is recognized.
rules.pass_when: When GPC=true is signaled, the site programmatically opts the user out of sale/sharing of non-essential data (consent state shows opt-out and advertising/sale requests are not made), and/or the policy explicitly states GPC is honored.
rules.fail_when: With GPC=true sent, non-essential/advertising trackers still fire and no opt-out is applied, and there is no acknowledgment of the GPC signal.
rules.evidence_hint: Capture the GPC=true browser flag, the resulting consent cookie/CMP state value, and the network panel showing suppressed advertising requests; or quote the policy line stating GPC is honored.

rules.title: Cross-domain third-party scripts audited and locked down
rules.what_to_look_for: All <script src="..."> with a cross-origin host (host differs from the page origin). For each, check it is justified (a recognizable analytics/CMP/functional vendor, not unknown), and hardened: presence of integrity="sha…" (SRI) and crossorigin attributes, and/or a Content-Security-Policy script-src allow-list restricting permitted origins. Flag a large or unexplained set of external script hosts.
rules.pass_when: Cross-domain scripts are limited to a justified vendor set AND locked down — protected by SRI (integrity attribute) and/or constrained by a CSP script-src allow-list naming the allowed hosts.
rules.fail_when: The page loads numerous or unidentified third-party scripts from arbitrary origins with no SRI and no CSP script-src restriction, leaving the script surface unaudited.
rules.evidence_hint: List the cross-origin <script src> hosts; quote any integrity= attributes and the Content-Security-Policy script-src directive (or note its absence).

rules.title: Cookieless privacy-respecting analytics in use
