rules.what_to_look_for: Analytics tooling identified in HTML/script src. Presence of cookieless, aggregate, EU-hostable analytics (e.g. Plausible 'plausible.io', Fathom 'usefathom.com', Simple Analytics 'simpleanalytics.com', Matomo configured cookieless, Cloudflare Web Analytics) rather than cookie-setting trackers (Google Analytics gtag/analytics.js, Facebook Pixel) that store personal identifiers.
rules.pass_when: The only analytics present are cookieless/aggregate privacy-respecting tools (no per-user cookies/identifiers), or no analytics is loaded at all.
rules.fail_when: The site uses cookie-based identifying analytics (e.g. Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel) as its analytics solution instead of a cookieless aggregate alternative.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the analytics <script src> (e.g. plausible.io/script.js or googletagmanager.com/gtag/js) identifying which class of analytics is loaded.

rules.title: Forms collect only necessary data
rules.what_to_look_for: Each <form> and its <input>/<select>/<textarea> fields. Compare the form's stated purpose against the personal-data fields it requests — flag fields not needed for that purpose (e.g. a newsletter signup asking for phone, postal address, date of birth, gender). Also check the privacy policy for a retention statement ('keep only as long as needed'). Required vs optional fields signaled via the required attribute.
rules.pass_when: Forms request only fields plausibly necessary for their stated purpose (extra personal fields marked optional or absent) AND a retention/keep-only-as-needed statement exists in the policy.
rules.fail_when: A form mandates personal-data fields irrelevant to its purpose (e.g. signup form requiring DOB, phone, address), or no data-retention limit is stated.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <form> purpose and its required <input> fields; cite any field excessive for the stated purpose and the policy's retention sentence (or its absence).

rules.title: 404 and 500 return correct status with helpful body and no stack leak
rules.what_to_look_for: Request a known-missing path (e.g. /this-page-does-not-exist-xyz) and inspect the response status line plus body. Look for HTTP status 404 (and, where a server-error route is reachable, 500) in the status line — NOT 200. In the rendered/returned body look for a plain-language explanation (e.g. 'Page not found', 'Something went wrong'), at least one navigation/recovery affordance (a link to home, search box, or back link — an <a href> or <form> in the error body), and the ABSENCE of leaked internals: no stack traces, file paths, framework/version banners, SQL errors, or exception class names.
rules.pass_when: Missing-path request returns status 404 (server-error route returns 500), the body contains a human-readable explanation AND at least one way-forward link/control, AND the body contains no stack trace, file path, framework version, or raw exception text.
rules.fail_when: Error response returns 200 (soft-404) or wrong status, OR the body lacks a plain-language explanation, OR offers no navigation/recovery link, OR leaks a stack trace, server path, framework/version string, or raw exception/SQL error.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the HTTP status line (e.g. 'HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found'), the explanatory sentence, the recovery link's <a href>, and any leaked stack-trace/path snippet if present.

rules.title: Maintenance responses use HTTP 503 with Retry-After
rules.what_to_look_for: When the site is in a maintenance/unavailable state, inspect the response status line and headers. Look for status code 503 (Service Unavailable) and a Retry-After response header carrying either a delay in seconds (e.g. 'Retry-After: 3600') or an HTTP-date (e.g. 'Retry-After: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT').
rules.pass_when: A maintenance/unavailable response returns HTTP status 503 AND includes a Retry-After header with a valid seconds value or HTTP-date.
rules.fail_when: Maintenance/unavailable page returns 200 or any non-503 status, OR returns 503 but omits the Retry-After header (or sends an invalid Retry-After value).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the status line ('HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable') and the 'Retry-After: <value>' header line.

rules.title: Service worker provides a cached offline fallback page
rules.what_to_look_for: In the live browser, check that a service worker is registered (navigator.serviceWorker.controller is non-null / a registration exists with an active worker) and that it caches an offline fallback. Then simulate offline (network disabled) and reload: the page should render a cached offline fallback (a real HTML page with content) rather than the browser's native 'No internet' dino/error page. Inspect the SW source for a fetch handler with a catch/offline-fallback (e.g. caches.match('/offline.html')).
rules.pass_when: A service worker is registered and active, AND loading a page while offline serves a cached HTML fallback page (site-controlled content) instead of the browser's default network-error screen.
rules.fail_when: No service worker is registered, OR the service worker has no offline fallback handler, OR reloading while offline shows the browser's native connection-error page instead of a cached fallback.
rules.evidence_hint: Capture the serviceWorker registration state (active worker scriptURL), the SW fetch-handler fallback line, and a screenshot of the offline page region showing site-controlled fallback content.

rules.title: Web app manifest links a JSON with required PWA fields
rules.what_to_look_for: In the raw HTML <head>, look for <link rel="manifest" href="...">. Fetch the referenced manifest and parse it as JSON; confirm it contains the keys name (or short_name), icons (a non-empty array with src and sizes), start_url, theme_color, and display (e.g. 'standalone', 'fullscreen', 'minimal-ui', or 'browser').
rules.pass_when: A <link rel="manifest"> exists, the target parses as valid JSON, and it includes name (or short_name), a non-empty icons array, start_url, theme_color, and display.
rules.fail_when: No <link rel="manifest"> in the HTML, OR the manifest fails to load/parse as JSON, OR it is missing any of: name/short_name, icons, start_url, theme_color, display.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <link rel="manifest" href> tag and the manifest JSON keys/values for name, icons, start_url, theme_color, and display.

rules.title: External uptime monitoring, RUM, and a separately-hosted status page exist
rules.what_to_look_for: Inspect the raw HTML for a Real User Monitoring (RUM) beacon — a <script> from a known RUM/monitoring vendor or first-party telemetry (e.g. New Relic browser agent, Datadog RUM, Sentry, Cloudflare beacon, Google Analytics/Web Vitals reporter). Then look for a status-page link (an <a href> or footer link to 'status.<domain>', statuspage.io, or a similarly-named host) and verify via DNS/host that the status page resolves to a DIFFERENT host/IP than the main site (so it survives a primary outage). External synthetic uptime monitoring is an operational control not directly visible in HTML — treat a published status page as its public proxy.
rules.pass_when: The HTML embeds a RUM/telemetry beacon AND links to a status page whose host resolves to a different host/domain (e.g. status.example.com or a third-party status provider) than the primary site.
rules.fail_when: No RUM/telemetry beacon is present in the HTML, OR there is no status-page link, OR the status page is served from the same host/origin as the main site (would be unreachable during a primary outage).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the RUM <script src> tag, the status-page <a href>, and note the status-page host resolving to a distinct domain/IP versus the main site.

rules.title: Use one consistent international URL pattern
rules.what_to_look_for: Determine the localisation URL strategy from the host and path: ccTLD (e.g. example.fr), language subdomain (e.g. fr.example.com), or path subdirectory (e.g. example.com/fr/). Cross-check the same signals in the hreflang alternates inside <link rel="alternate" hreflang=...> hrefs and any visible locale links — all locale URLs should follow the identical pattern.
rules.pass_when: Every locale-specific URL (page URL plus all hreflang alternate hrefs) follows a single consistent pattern: all ccTLD, OR all subdomain, OR all subdirectory — never a mix.
rules.fail_when: Locale URLs mix patterns (e.g. one locale on a subdirectory /de/ while another uses a subdomain fr.example.com or a ccTLD example.es), so no single strategy is identifiable.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote 2-3 alternate hreflang hrefs showing the host/path shape, and name the detected pattern (ccTLD / subdomain / subdirectory).

rules.title: Declare reciprocal hreflang alternates with valid BCP 47 codes
rules.what_to_look_for: In <head>, find <link rel="alternate" hreflang="..." href="..."> tags. Verify each hreflang value is a valid BCP 47 tag (language or language-region, e.g. "en", "en-GB", "pt-BR", or "x-default"). Check for a self-referencing alternate pointing to the current page and that alternates are reciprocal (each listed alternate should point back to the others).
rules.pass_when: Multiple <link rel="alternate" hreflang> tags exist with syntactically valid BCP 47 codes, include a self-reference for the current page, and form a reciprocal set (alternates reference each other).
rules.fail_when: hreflang tags are absent on a multilingual site, use malformed codes (e.g. "en_US", "english", invalid region), omit the self-reference, or are non-reciprocal/one-directional.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the full <link rel="alternate" hreflang=...> block from <head>, highlighting the hreflang values and the self-reference.

rules.title: Translate page metadata, not just body copy
rules.what_to_look_for: Inspect <title>, <meta name="description">, Open Graph tags (og:title, og:description, og:locale), JSON-LD structured data text values, and image alt attributes. On a localised page these must be in the page's declared language (matching <html lang>), not left in the default/source language.
rules.pass_when: <title>, meta description, OG tags, JSON-LD text fields, and img alt attributes are all in the page's declared <html lang> language, and og:locale matches that locale.
rules.fail_when: Body text is localised but title/description/OG/JSON-LD/alt remain in a different (source/default) language, or og:locale does not match <html lang>.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <title>, <meta name="description">, og:locale and one img alt, noting the language each is written in versus the <html lang> value.

rules.title: Provide hreflang alternates via xhtml:link in the XML sitemap
rules.what_to_look_for: In sitemap.xml, check that the urlset declares xmlns:xhtml and that each <url> entry contains <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="..." href="..."/> elements listing all locale alternates (including a self-reference), as an alternative to in-head <link> tags.
rules.pass_when: Sitemap urlset declares the xhtml namespace and <url> entries carry <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang=...> alternates with valid BCP 47 codes including self-references.
rules.fail_when: Sitemap is absent, omits the xhtml namespace, or <url> entries lack any <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang> alternate annotations.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote one <url> block from sitemap.xml showing the xhtml:link alternate elements and their hreflang values.

rules.title: Avoid automatic IP- or Accept-Language-based language redirects
rules.what_to_look_for: Request the root/locale-neutral URL with differing Accept-Language headers (and note geolocation/IP). Inspect for a 301/302/307 redirect Location header that forces a locale path/subdomain/ccTLD based solely on IP geolocation or Accept-Language, with no way to stay on the requested URL.
rules.pass_when: The requested URL is served directly (200) without a forced locale redirect, OR locale is offered via a non-blocking banner/suggestion while the requested URL still loads.
rules.fail_when: A 3xx response with a Location header automatically redirects the user to a locale-specific URL based on IP geolocation or Accept-Language, trapping users/crawlers on a single locale.
rules.evidence_hint: Capture the request URL + Accept-Language sent and the response status line plus Location header showing the forced redirect.

rules.title: Mark inline foreign-language passages with lang
rules.what_to_look_for: Find text passages, phrases, or quotations written in a language different from the page's <html lang>. Each such span/element must carry its own lang attribute with the correct BCP 47 code (WCAG 3.1.2 Language of Parts). Proper names and technical terms in the page's primary language are exempt.
rules.pass_when: Every passage in a language other than the document's primary language is wrapped in an element bearing a correct lang attribute (e.g. ...).
rules.fail_when: Foreign-language passages appear in the body without a surrounding element carrying the correct lang attribute, while the document <html lang> stays the primary language.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote a foreign-language passage and show whether its wrapping element has a lang attribute and what value.

rules.title: Label each language switcher option in its own language
rules.what_to_look_for: Locate the language/locale switcher control (nav, select, or link list). Each option's label must be written as the endonym in its own language (e.g. "Deutsch", "Français", "日本語" — not "German"/"French"), each link/option should carry a lang and hreflang attribute, and the control must not rely on country flags to denote a language.
rules.pass_when: Switcher options use each locale's own endonym as the label, carry correct lang/hreflang attributes, and identify languages by name rather than by flag icons.
rules.fail_when: Switcher labels are all in one language, options lack lang/hreflang attributes, or languages are represented only by flag images.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the switcher markup (option labels + lang/hreflang attrs) and note any flag used as the sole language indicator.

rules.title: Set dir=rtl and use CSS logical properties for RTL scripts
rules.what_to_look_for: For pages in RTL languages (lang ar, he, fa, ur), check that <html> or the relevant container has dir="rtl". Inspect the CSS for layout/spacing using logical properties (margin-inline, padding-inline, inset-inline, text-align: start/end) rather than hard-coded physical left/right that breaks under RTL.
rules.pass_when: RTL-language pages declare dir="rtl" on <html> (or the content container) and rely on CSS logical properties so layout mirrors correctly.
rules.fail_when: An RTL-language page (lang ar/he/fa/ur) lacks dir="rtl", or its CSS uses physical left/right properties that prevent correct mirroring.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the <html lang dir> opening tag and one CSS rule showing logical (or offending physical) directional properties.

rules.title: Configure writing-mode and line breaking for CJK and Thai
rules.what_to_look_for: For vertical-script content, check computed CSS writing-mode (e.g. vertical-rl). For CJK/Thai text, check computed line-break and word-break (e.g. line-break: strict, word-break: normal/keep-all) so lines wrap per script rules. Render to confirm characters wrap and orient correctly without clipping or mid-word breaks.
rules.pass_when: Vertical content has the appropriate writing-mode applied, and CJK/Thai text uses correct computed line-break/word-break so wrapping follows script conventions.
rules.fail_when: Vertical text lacks writing-mode (renders horizontally), or CJK/Thai text breaks improperly (clipped, broken mid-character, or wrapped against script rules) due to missing line-break/word-break.
rules.evidence_hint: Screenshot the rendered CJK/vertical text region and quote the computed writing-mode / line-break / word-break values.

rules.title: Format dates, numbers, currency and units per locale
rules.what_to_look_for: Inspect rendered dates, numbers, currencies, and units for locale-correct formatting (decimal/grouping separators, date order, currency symbol/placement, unit system) consistent with the page locale — ideally produced by the Intl API (Intl.DateTimeFormat / Intl.NumberFormat) and matching server-side locale.
rules.pass_when: Displayed dates/numbers/currency/units use the formatting conventions of the page's declared locale, consistent between server-rendered and client-rendered output.
rules.fail_when: Formatting uses a fixed/foreign locale regardless of page language (e.g. US 1,234.56 or MM/DD/YYYY on a German page), or server and client formats disagree.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote a rendered date, number, and currency value and state the expected locale formatting versus what is shown.

rules.title: Apply CLDR plural categories for grammatical number
rules.what_to_look_for: Inspect strings involving counts/quantities for correct grammatical number per the locale's CLDR plural categories (zero/one/two/few/many/other) — ideally driven by Intl.PluralRules — rather than naive English-style if(n==1) singular/plural logic.
rules.pass_when: Count-dependent strings select the grammatically correct form for the locale's CLDR plural category across representative counts.
rules.fail_when: Pluralisation uses hard-coded singular/plural English logic that produces wrong forms for the locale (e.g. ignores few/many categories in Slavic/Arabic locales).
rules.evidence_hint: Quote a count-bearing string at a few representative numbers and note the locale's required CLDR category versus the rendered form.

rules.title: Represent internationalised domain names as Punycode with anti-spoofing
rules.what_to_look_for: For non-ASCII (IDN) domains, verify the registrable domain resolves via its ASCII-compatible Punycode (xn--) A-label in DNS, and check for homograph/anti-spoofing hygiene — labels should not mix confusable scripts (mixed Latin/Cyrillic) that enable spoofing.
rules.pass_when: IDN domains are registered/resolvable as their xn-- Punycode A-label and labels avoid mixed confusable scripts that enable homograph spoofing.
rules.fail_when: A non-ASCII domain is used without a valid Punycode (xn--) representation, or labels mix confusable scripts creating a homograph-spoofing risk.
rules.evidence_hint: Quote the Unicode domain alongside its xn-- Punycode form and the DNS record confirming resolution; note any mixed-script labels.
